title: Ford Just Delivered Bad News for Tesla Investors
author: Marc Guberti
description: Ford announced it will achieve point-to-point autonomy by 2028 with Apple executives working on the technology, positioning itself to enter the robotaxi market. This threatens Tesla's dominance in robotaxis, one of the key growth drivers justifying Tesla's extremely high P/E ratio of ~300. As traditional automakers like Ford, Toyota, and Volkswagen enter the robotaxi space, competition will intensify and pressure Tesla's future margins and growth rates in this sector.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Tesla faces increasing competition in robotaxis from Ford and other automakers. With a P/E ratio of ~300, Tesla has no margin for error and relies heavily on robotaxi and humanoid robot success. Rising competition threatens growth rates and profit margins in this critical segment.

title: Famous Investor Michael Burry Is Short Nvidia, Palantir, and Tesla. Why I'd Buy 1 of the Stocks, Hold Another, and Sell the Third.
author: Geoffrey Seiler
description: Michael Burry is short on Nvidia, Palantir, and Tesla, but analyst Geoffrey Seiler disagrees with his bearish stance on all three. Despite Burry's concerns about AI spending slowdowns, Seiler recommends buying Nvidia due to strong capex trends and attractive valuation. Palantir is rated a hold despite high valuations, given its rapid growth and strong net dollar retention. Tesla is recommended as a sell due to loss of regulatory credits, weak auto sales, and execution risks in robotaxi and robotics ventures.

title: Tim Cook Will Host His Last Earnings Call as Apple CEO on July 30. Is the Stock a Buy Now?
author: Geoffrey Seiler
description: Tim Cook will host his final earnings call as Apple CEO on July 30 as the company reports strong iPhone sales and service revenue growth. While Apple has an excellent business model and will benefit from recent price increases under incoming CEO John Ternus, the analyst recommends waiting for a better entry point due to the stock's elevated valuation with a forward P/E ratio over 35x and potential margin pressure from rising memory prices.
